html:
Iranian pastoralists is the map's label for the herding peoples of the central Asian steppe from about 1500 to 700 BCE, who spoke early Iranian languages. They came out of the Sintashta and Andronovo world, where the Indo-Iranian languages are thought to have taken shape.

They raised cattle, sheep and horses, and drove light chariots with spoked wheels. Some groups moved south into the oases of the Oxus civilisation and on to the Iranian plateau. By the 800s BCE Assyrian records name the Medes and Persians in western Iran.

The oldest texts of Zoroastrianism, the Avesta, come from this herding world; they praise cattle and good pasture and fight raiders. The groups who stayed on the steppe became the Scythians and Saka, who rode out of the same lands in the following centuries.
